### Observed differences

- In the later window, the elapsed time between consecutive completions of A23 and A27 is roughly half of what it was before: the average gap fell from about 0.93 hours (median about 0.93, middle half between about 0.83 and 1.02 hours) to about 0.46 hours (median about 0.46, middle half between about 0.41 and 0.51 hours), a reduction of about 0.47 hours. [TWAIT001]
- The shift is uniform rather than driven by a few long gaps: every quartile dropped by roughly 0.42–0.51 hours and the spread halved (standard deviation from about 0.14 to about 0.07 hours), so later gaps are systematically shorter, not just more variable. [TWAIT001]
- The comparison rests on a similar amount of data in both windows — 58 measured gaps before and 62 after, meaning the pair occurred in roughly 30 in 100 traces in each window — and a difference of this size exceeds about 999.5 in 1000 random re-splits of the pooled data. [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a change in timing between activities A23 and A27: in the later window, the time elapsed between their consecutive completions was consistently about half of the earlier value, falling from about 0.93 to about 0.46 hours across the whole distribution. [TWAIT001]

The supporting signs are that the indicator measures exactly this pair directly, the shift is consistent across the entire distribution rather than confined to a tail, the pair was observed at a similar rate in both windows (58 vs 62 gaps, roughly 30 in 100 traces each), and the difference is larger than in about 999.5 of 1000 reference comparisons. At the screening level, the time family produced 1 qualifying item where about 0.011 would be expected if nothing had changed — many times the chance expectation — while control flow produced none (0 items against about 0.28 expected), so the difference shows up as pure timing with no detectable structural counterpart. [TWAIT001]

Limitations: this measure captures elapsed time between consecutive completion events and cannot show whether the reduction lies in waiting or in processing between the two completions; and with only one activity pair flagged, a shift in the mix of cases containing this pair cannot be fully ruled out, although the uniform shift and stable prevalence argue against it. [TWAIT001]
